transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that for the past year or so, I feel like I’m always doing something—puttering around, fixing things, arranging things, signing up to help with one more thing. Even at 87, I have a hard time just sitting down and being still.
When you notice yourself needing to keep busy like this, do you also feel worried or on edge, or do you mostly feel unusually energetic and upbeat?

I’m not really sure it’s worry. I don’t feel especially on edge, and I wouldn’t say I’m unusually upbeat either. It’s more just… I notice I’m moving from one thing to the next and not settling very well.
Have you started or changed any new medications, especially any antipsychotic, anti-nausea, or other prescription drugs, around the time this restlessness began?
I don’t think so. I can’t recall starting anything new around then, but I’d have to check my medication list to be sure.

When you're moving around like this, do you notice any movements that happen on their own—like your mouth, tongue, or limbs twitching or moving without you meaning them to—or is it more that you feel an inner urge to keep moving that you're choosing to act on?

I don’t notice my mouth or tongue moving on their own or anything like that. It’s more like this ants-in-my-chair feeling. Like at senior center meetings or sitting through church announcements, I just have to shift around, get up for coffee, or straighten papers so I can get through it.
Have you noticed any recent unexplained weight loss, feeling unusually warm or sweaty, a racing heart, or a tremor in your hands over this past year?
No, I can’t say I’ve noticed anything like that. My weight seems about the same, and I haven’t noticed being unusually sweaty or my heart racing. I don’t think I’ve had a hand tremor either.
When you get up and move around or pace, does that restless feeling go away for a bit, and then come back once you sit or lie down again?

Yes, for a little while. If I get up for coffee or straighten some papers, it helps me get through it. But once I’m sitting again, especially at those meetings or during church announcements, that ants-in-my-chair feeling comes back and I start shifting around again.
Do you notice this restless, need-to-move feeling specifically in your legs, and does it tend to get worse in the evening or at night compared to earlier in the day?
I’m not really sure it’s just in my legs. It feels more like my whole body wants to move or I need to shift around. I haven’t noticed it being worse in the evening or at night, not specifically.
Could you check your medication list for me—are you currently taking, or have you recently taken, any antipsychotic medications or anti-nausea drugs such as metoclopramide or prochlorperazine?
I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’m taking anything like that, but I’d have to look at my medication list to be sure.
In the past year, have you been given or prescribed any medication for nausea, dizziness, or vertigo—even if you don't remember exactly what it was called?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember being given anything for nausea or dizziness this past year, but I’d have to check my records or medication list to be certain.

Aside from feeling like you need to keep moving, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about several different things—like your health, family, or finances—and have trouble controlling those worries?
I don’t think so, not in that way. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed it being excessive or hard to control.

Would it be possible for you to bring in your actual pill bottles or medication list to our next visit, or have a family member check for you, so we can see if any antipsychotic or anti-nausea medication is listed?
Yes, I can do that. I’ll bring my pill bottles or my medication list next time, and if I’m not sure, I can ask a family member to help me check.

When you feel that urge to get up and move, do you also notice an uncomfortable inner tension or distress driving it, or does it feel more like a purely physical restlessness without any accompanying emotional discomfort?

It feels more physical, I think. Like when I’m at the senior center meetings or sitting through church announcements, I get this ants-in-my-chair feeling. I’ll shift around, or get up for coffee, or straighten papers just to get through sitting there. I wouldn’t say it’s really emotional distress driving it.
Even if you haven't started any new medications, has the dose of any medication you already take been increased in the past year?
I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed any dose changes myself, but I’d have to check the bottles or my list to be certain.
Would you say this restless, need-to-move feeling is with you pretty much all day long, or does it mainly show up when you're stuck sitting still for a while, like at those meetings or church?

It mainly shows up when I’m stuck sitting still for a while. Like at the senior center meetings or during church announcements, I get that ants-in-my-chair feeling and I have to shift around, stand up for coffee, or fiddle with papers just to get through it. It’s not really all day long.

Do you notice this same need to get up and move even when you're doing something you enjoy and have to sit still for, like watching a favorite TV show or a good movie, or does it really only happen during things you find boring or tedious, like meetings or announcements?

It’s mostly during the boring sitting-still things, like the senior center meetings or church announcements. That’s when I get that ants-in-my-chair feeling and start shifting around, getting up for coffee, or straightening papers just to get through it.
If you really try, can you sit still and resist the urge to get up or move, or does it feel like you absolutely have to move no matter how hard you try to stay still?

If I really make myself, I can usually stay seated, but it’s uncomfortable. I’ll be shifting around, fiddling with papers, that sort of thing. At the senior center or during church announcements, it feels like I need to do something to get through it, even if I don’t always fully get up.
Have your family members or friends ever commented that they notice you fidgeting or moving around more than usual, even when you didn't feel like you were doing anything unusual?

Yes, sometimes. At the senior center meetings or during church announcements, people have noticed me shifting around or getting up for coffee. I don’t always realize I’m doing it that much—I just feel like I need to move a little or straighten papers to get through sitting there.

Do you notice this same need to get up and move when you're alone at home, just sitting quietly by yourself with nothing in particular going on, or does it really only come up in these public situations like meetings or church?

It’s more in those public situations where I’m expected to sit still, like the senior center meetings or church announcements. At home, if I’m just sitting by myself, I don’t notice it as much. But in those settings, I get that ants-in-my-chair feeling and end up shifting around, getting coffee, or straightening papers to get through it.
